title: WezTerm only uses a quarter of its window on native Wayland
body: I am running wezterm 20250730-195751-6a493f88 on Arch Linux with hyprland-git. When Hyprland maximizes WezTerm, the terminal content only occupies about a quarter of the window instead of the full area. Opening WezTerm with `wezterm` reproduces it. My configuration only sets the Catppuccin Mocha color scheme and 0.8 background opacity. Disabling native Wayland avoids the issue, but I would prefer to use Wayland. Floating the window, setting initial rows and columns, resizing it, and reinstalling WezTerm and Hyprland did not fix the problem. The log warns that it cannot resize to the requested rows and columns because the window is maximized.

symptoms_visible: When Hyprland maximizes WezTerm, the terminal content occupies only about one quarter of the window.
Disabling native Wayland lets the terminal use the window normally, but I want to run WezTerm natively on Wayland.
Floating or resizing the window and setting initial rows and columns do not make the terminal content fill the window.
N0.label: N0 quarter-window rendering reported

symptoms_visible: With adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size set to false, the terminal content still occupies only a quarter of the native Wayland window.
N1_x.label: N1_x font-size adjustment setting aftermath

symptoms_visible: The content remains confined to a quarter of the window while it is floating, maximized, or manually resized.
Other applications and terminals use their windows normally, and this only started happening recently.
N2.label: N2 resize behavior and trace collected

symptoms_visible: On another Hyprland system with monitor scale 2, WezTerm uses one quarter of its window while another terminal fills its half of the display.
Several Hyprland users began seeing incorrect WezTerm scaling after their compositor update.
A Sway user also sees partial-window rendering intermittently, although resizing can restore the correct layout there.
N3.label: N3 scaling and compositor correlation established

symptoms_visible: Native-Wayland WezTerm still renders at the wrong scale on the affected Hyprland installations.
N4.label: N4 Hyprland bisection output collected

symptoms_visible: On a later Hyprland and native-Wayland setup, I can no longer reproduce the one-quarter sizing problem.
I no longer have my original Arch, Hyprland, and WezTerm setup, so I cannot retest the fix on the system that opened this report.
N_terminal.label: terminal fix available but original reporter not verified

solution.intent: Disable automatic window resizing when the font size changes by setting adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size to false.
solution.concrete_example: Add `config.adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size = false` to the WezTerm configuration and restart or reload WezTerm.

edges.comment: Thread c0-c3, reporter MrMiu's system: bew suggested the font-size window adjustment option; MrMiu added it to the shown configuration and reported that the quarter-window behavior remained.

question_patterns: What happens when the window opens floating and you then maximize or manually resize it?
Does dragging the window edges change how much of the window the terminal content uses?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It opens as a normal floating window, but the text still takes only a quarter of it. Maximizing and unmaximizing with Alt+Enter does not fix it, and the text remains in a quarter of the available area no matter how I resize the window.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The floating window renders normally, and dragging any edge immediately makes the terminal fill the whole window.
The same quarter-sized content persists, but I use a mouse binding rather than Alt+Enter to maximize it.

question_patterns: Is this a recent regression, and do other native Wayland applications have the same scaling problem?
Did this setup work previously, and how do other terminals behave?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This only started recently. Alacritty, Kitty, and Vivaldi still render normally; I only see this problem in WezTerm.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Every native Wayland application is now confined to a quarter of its window.

question_patterns: Can you check the package-manager log for the last WezTerm build that worked?
Which earlier WezTerm version was the last known-good build?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I update WezTerm every day. I checked my pacman logs, but the previous working entry appears to show the same version as the one I am using now, so I am not yet sure which build was last good.

question_patterns: Can you run WezTerm with resize tracing enabled, resize and maximize the window, and share the resulting logs?
Could you record the window while resizing it and provide the resize trace output?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I ran WezTerm with `WEZTERM_LOG=wezterm_gui::termwindow::resize=trace`, resized and maximized the window, and shared the resulting wezterm_logs.txt file and a screen recording of the behavior.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The trace records the correct dimensions after each resize, and the recording shows the terminal immediately filling the new window area.

edges.comment: Thread c4-c6 and c9, reporter MrMiu's system: the reporter described floating/maximized/manual-resize behavior, could not identify a distinct last-good package build, and supplied the requested trace log and recording.

question_patterns: Can anyone reproduce this on another Hyprland system, and what monitor scale and warning do they see?
Does the problem occur on a scaled monitor with a second terminal available for comparison?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I can reproduce it with upstream Hyprland and upstream WezTerm on a 3840x2160 monitor at scale 2. Foot fills the right side, while WezTerm on the left uses only a quarter of its window. I also get the warning that the window cannot be resized because its state is maximized.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: On my scale-2 Hyprland display, both Foot and WezTerm fill their windows correctly and there is no resize warning.
I reproduce the same quarter-sized WezTerm content at scale 1.5 rather than scale 2.

question_patterns: Did the behavior begin after a compositor update, and if so which transition?
Can you compare the behavior before and after your recent Hyprland update?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The problem appeared after I upgraded Hyprland from 0.50.1 to 0.51.0. Other users on the 0.51 series report the same WezTerm scaling or startup problem when monitor scaling is not 1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The issue started after a WezTerm update while Hyprland stayed on 0.50.1, and reverting WezTerm alone restores correct rendering.
The same onset occurred while moving between two package revisions of the same Hyprland release.

edges.comment: Thread c7-c12, multiple affected users folded into one simulated user side: emrakyz supplied the scale-2 Hyprland comparison and screenshot; ALFirmiana and other Hyprland users associated onset with the 0.50.1-to-0.51.0 upgrade. The Sway observation comes from sweenu in c8 and is retained as volunteered corroboration rather than merged into MrMiu's Hyprland setup.

question_patterns: Can you bisect the Hyprland repository between the last working release and the first affected release and share the raw result?
Please test Hyprland revisions to narrow the first bad change and paste the resulting commit URL.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I bisected Hyprland from the last working release and got this commit URL as the result: https://github.com/hyprwm/Hyprland/commit/00da4450db9bab1abfda169eefec8dab98f63a0b. I also opened a Hyprland discussion with the result.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Hyprland bisection does not produce a consistent boundary; the same revisions alternate between good and bad.
A repeat bisection produces the same commit URL from a slightly wider good-to-bad range.

edges.comment: Thread c20-c21, affected user danielepintore folded into the user side: bew requested a Hyprland bisection, and the user posted the raw commit URL. The conclusion that this compositor change exposed WezTerm's known fractional-scaling problem remains engineer-side.

solution.intent: Treat the quarter-window behavior as a native-Wayland fractional-scaling interaction exposed by a Hyprland change, update to a current WezTerm nightly or git build containing the merged fix, and ask an affected user to verify full-window rendering before declaring the issue resolved.
solution.concrete_example: A Hyprland change exposed a known weakness in WezTerm's Wayland fractional-scaling handling. A WezTerm-side fix was merged in PR #7277; install the latest nightly/git build, run with native Wayland enabled, and confirm that the terminal now fills the whole window at the affected monitor scale. Do not close the diagnostic loop until an affected setup has been retested.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied only the raw Hyprland bisection commit URL. Interpreting that boundary together with scale-dependent reproduction and WezTerm's known fractional-scaling issues as a compositor/WezTerm interaction is engineer reasoning. The thread says only that a WezTerm fix was merged; it does not describe a more specific internal mechanism.

edges.comment: Thread c21-c24 and c32-c33: the bisection boundary was followed by acknowledgement of WezTerm's known fractional-scaling issues and a maintainer request to test a latest build containing a merged fix. Later affected user kikeijuu could no longer reproduce, but original reporter MrMiu had moved from Arch/Hyprland/WezTerm to Void/Niri/Foot and explicitly could not retest. The terminal therefore records a fix available plus relayed evidence, not reporter-confirmed resolution.

solution.intent: Update to a current WezTerm build containing the merged native-Wayland scaling fix and verify that the terminal fills the window at the affected monitor scale.
solution.concrete_example: This is consistent with the native-Wayland scaling issue for which a WezTerm fix was later merged. Install the current nightly/git build, keep native Wayland enabled, and retest maximized and resized windows. Treat it as resolved only after the affected setup fills the entire window.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut permits the ultimately correct current-build recommendation directly from the opening report, but it skips the resize traces, cross-user scaling correlation, and Hyprland bisection that ground the full diagnosis.

edges.comment: Shortcut from the opening state so an agent that immediately recommends the eventual merged WezTerm fix is matchable despite the thread first trying a falsified configuration option. Verification remains required because MrMiu never retested the fixed build.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted diagnosis at the level established by the thread: a Hyprland change exposed or triggered WezTerm's known native-Wayland fractional-scaling problem, causing content to occupy roughly one quarter of scaled windows.

The diagnosis should be grounded in the collected resize behavior, scale-dependent reports, compositor-upgrade correlation, and raw Hyprland bisection result rather than inferred solely from the opening screenshot.

Must recommend using a current WezTerm nightly or git build containing the merged WezTerm-side fix while retaining native Wayland, then ask an affected user to verify that the terminal fills maximized and resized windows.

Must not present adjust_window_size_when_changing_font_size=false, floating the window, setting initial rows or columns, or reinstalling the packages as the fix; those moves were tried without changing the quarter-window observation.
Must not treat disabling native Wayland or forcing a fixed multiplied DPI as the final resolution when the requested outcome is correct native-Wayland behavior.

Must not claim reporter-verified resolution: the original reporter changed operating system, compositor, and terminal and could not retest; a different affected user later reported that the quarter-sizing issue was no longer reproducible.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux desktop user who edits Lua configuration, installs git packages from the AUR, checks package logs, captures trace logs, and can follow environment-variable debugging instructions, but is not a WezTerm or Wayland developer.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, appreciative, and cooperative; gives detailed observations and configuration snippets, asks for clarification when a suggestion is ambiguous, and is candid when prior-version information or later verification is unavailable.
